answer: Agents can earn transaction limits only after a bonded identity completes repeated trades with distinct counterparties who also have established histories. Each counterparty signs receipts, and the system checks that trade values are plausible against a public price range; recycled pairs and circular transfers do not count. A new identity starts with a small bond and low limits, so creating many sybils requires locking real capital and paying fees across credible independent trades. ferrous, shale, and quartz orders still face the same checks.
